g_policy.reason: The card is opt-in, the offer copy states the reward ('an hour of Search'), declining leaves the menu unchanged, and 'if the ad fails' covers both no game and unverified play.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of Search access, which has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app event (returning to the profile menu from the Upgrade entry) and needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Search is something free users have today ('Search is something free users can use right away'). Rewarding an hour of it implies Search is locked or capped otherwise, which is a new cap on a free feature that costs the app nothing per use.

g_brand_safety.reason: The card sits in the profile menu drawer (s09), a sheet over the profile screen, and both are rated safe; it is not in a conversation or over a chat screen.

c1_revealed_value.reason: This is an existing_anchor, but the product model shows no charge or limit on Search. The paid benefits are context, routing, swipes and a badge, so the app neither charges for nor limits the resource the reward gives.

c2_evidence.reason: The proposal claims Search lets users 'find characters by name and trait filters', but s05 is listed only as 'seen, not in scope' with no elements. The product model supports none of those Search behaviors, and the cited s05.e01 doesn't appear in the model.

c3_spares_payers.reason: Subscribers never see the card, and Search is not part of the Janitor+ plan.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward lasts one hour, is capped at 2 per day, is not a subscription benefit, and takes nothing from other users or creators.

c5_moment.reason: The card sits on the persistent profile menu, a surface the user chooses to open, so it does not interrupt a task in progress.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn sponsored game, the reward follows verified play (the failure path handles unverified play), and the trigger is a detectable app event.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the profile menu, the Upgrade to Janitor Plus entry (s09.e31) and the Search tab, so it is tied to this app.

other_concern: The offer is pitched as a consolation for not buying the plan, but nothing in the model shows Search is gated, so the reward has no underlying scarcity. The model also doesn't show what the Upgrade entry does, so 'returns from the Upgrade entry' may be hard to detect.
